annotations.text:
Pick a direction.

All three show the same library so the comparison is fair, and all use your real disks — Project-X, Deluxe Paint IV, 9 Fingers, Workbench 3.1.

Cover images are generated placeholders: real box art comes from Hasheous/IGDB at ingest, and this is genuinely what a disk with no art will look like.

A — Workbench Revival
Dense, filter-forward, Amiga orange/blue on cool slate, 3px radii, monospace metadata.

Best at 1,884 titles. Trade-off: least cinematic.

B — Cinema
Poster-forward, near-black, amber, big display type, hero + rows.

Most impact per screen. Trade-off: shows ~12 titles where A shows 40 — weak for a large library.

C — Console
Monospace table, keyboard-first, sortable, SHA visible.

Fastest to find one disk among thousands. Trade-off: box art is decorative, not the point.

The three functional screens, drawn in Direction A. These do not change much if you pick B or C — the layout logic is the same, only the skin differs.

Everything shown is grounded in what the hardware actually does: the 8 MB PSRAM budget, the FAT12 RAM disk, the /ADF/<Game>/ tree the firmware reads, and the 512-byte .nfo limit.
